chunks: Safwan narrated from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Saʿd, who said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about the Gate of al-Ṣafā, and I said: Our companions have differed about it. Some of them say it is the one adjacent to the water station, and some of them say it is the one facing the Black Stone. So he said: “It is the one facing the Black Stone, and the one adjacent to the water station is a newly introduced one; Dāwūd made it and Dāwūd opened it.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابَنَا: the Shia companions or associates who differed on the issue
key_terms.السِّقَايَةَ: the water station or place of providing water near the sanctuary
key_terms.الْحَجَرَ الْأَسْوَدَ: the Black Stone, used here as a landmark for identifying the gate
key_terms.بَابِ الصَّفَا: the Gate of al-Ṣafā under discussion in the hadith
key_terms.دَاوُدُ: the person said to have made and opened the newer gate
key_terms.مُحْدَثٌ: newly introduced; not part of the original arrangement

ai.seo_question: Which gate is meant by Bāb al-Ṣafā according to Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies the correct location of Bāb al-Ṣafā in the context of tawaf and clarifies a disagreement among the companions. Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام states that the correct gate is the one facing al-Ḥajar al-Aswad, while the one near the water station was a later construction.
